name: Woody fragrances

lead:
Woody fragrances are a major scent family built around notes such as cedar, sandalwood and vetiver, often with spice or amber. They are worn to smell clean, warm and put-together, which many people treat as part of overall grooming and presentation.
The appearance payoff is indirect: scent does not change how someone looks, but forum users describe it as shaping how they are perceived and as earning compliments. The discussion is mostly personal experience.

paras: Men on forums describe choosing a woody cologne as a signature scent, sometimes with a fresher option for day and a spicier one for evening, and pairing it with a matching deodorant stick. Longevity is a common selection criterion, with some posters saying their picks can still be smelled the next morning.
Fragrance ingredients can cause skin irritation or contact allergy in some people, and strong scents can bother others in shared spaces. Reactions to any specific perfume vary from person to person.

angle.text: Wearers use woody scents as the finishing layer of a grooming routine. They describe compliments and a more put-together impression, though this is reported experience rather than measured outcome.

lead: Woody is one of the main scent families in Michael Edwards' fragrance wheel, alongside floral, amber and fresh. Its subfamilies include woody amber (for example sandalwood and patchouli), woods (aromatic woods and vetiver), mossy woods and dry woods [1].

In men's grooming, woody colognes are chosen for a warm, grounded, 'classic' impression. Forum users on T Nation mention woody-spicy designer scents such as Terre d'Hermes and Yves Saint Laurent's Jazz as long-lasting everyday picks and report compliments on them [2][3].
No published trial has looked at woody scents specifically as a way of improving perceived attractiveness; the evidence base here is anecdotal.

paras: The fragrance wheel groups scents into families whose neighbours share similar odour traits, and its authors note that the boundaries are rough and overlap across sources [1].
Sandalwood and vetiver are cited as typical woody ingredients in the wheel's description; users also associate cedar with the family [1][2].

On T Nation, men swapping cologne recommendations describe a woody-spicy scent as long-lasting and 'classic', and say they buy the matching deodorant stick [2]. Another poster wears a fresher woody scent by day and a spicier one at night, and reports compliments on both [3].

lore.intro: Fragrance threads on T Nation treat cologne as part of everyday grooming rather than as a dedicated looksmaxxing method [2][3].

claims.claim: A woody signature scent draws compliments
